newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MILAN BEAT GOTHENBURG TO KEEP HOPES HIGH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN BEAT GOTHENBURG TO KEEP HOPES HIGH.

text.p: Substitute Roberto Baggio scored a last-minute goal for AC Milan on Wednesday as the Italians beat Sweden's IFK Gothenburg 4-2 in their do-or-die Champions' League group D match.
Milan, beaten in two of their three matches to date, desperately needed to beat Gothenburg to stave off an early exit from the competition they have won five times.
The win left Milan second in their group on six points, behind Porto on 12 but ahead of Gothenburg and Rosenborg of Norway who both have three points.

The home team, whose unimpressive league form was demonstrated by Fiorentina's 1-0 win over them last weekend, took the lead after just three minutes through Croat Zvonimir Boban and then went 2-0 up after another 10 minutes.
Demetrio Albertini converted a 13th minute penalty after Marco Simone, whose perfect cross set up Boban's earlier headed goal, had been felled by Mikael Nilsson.
Normally, that would have been enough to guarantee Milan's victory and allow the fans room to relax.
But Milan have had one of the leakier defences in serie A this season and Gothenburg took advantage, with Stefan Pettersson hitting the post in the 19th minute.
The Swedes, who beat Milan 2-1 in Gothenburg two weeks ago, continued to push forward and were rewarded when unmarked Jesper Blomqvist slotted home in the 26th minute.
Andreas Andersson found the equaliser in the 32nd in a goalmouth scramble following a corner, with Pettersson again hitting the upright before the ball went in.

"We're not used to letting in two goals in succession at Milan," said owner Silvio Berlusconi. "We've always had the strongest defence around which allowed us to dictate the results. But that's not the case any more."
The crowd, fearing yet another collapse by the home team, began whistling as Milan's concentration vanished.
Uruguayan coach Oscar Tabarez, standing on the touchline and exhorting his players to calm down, was rewarded when Tomas Locatelli seized the lead again.
Simone crossed from the right and Locatelli outpaced the defenders to the ball and fired home.
"After it was 2-0 the ghosts came back to haunt us but fortunately they went away again. We dominated the game in the second half and deserved to win," said Tabarez.
"The players were too nervous and in those conditions it's hard to play good football," he added.
Both teams had their chances in the second half but the decisive move only came after Italy's 1994 World Cup star Baggio came on as a substitute in the 63rd minute.
Baggio's entry was greeted by a roar from the fans and he delivered the goods when he hit home from close range a beautiful low cross from George Weah in the last minute.
"We played well, I'm proud of my players but Milan is a very strong team," said Gothenburg coach Mats Jingblad.
Teams:

Milan: 1-Sebastiano Rossi, 2-Christian Panucci, 3-Paolo Maldini, 11-Alessandro Costacurta, 8-Marcel Desailly, 16-Tomas Locatelli (24-Stefanio Eranio, 46), 4-Demetrio Albertini, 20-Zvonimir Boban, 22-Edgar Davids, 9-George Weah, 23-Marco Simone (18-Roberto Baggio, 63).

IFK Gothenburg: 1-Thomas Ravelli, 22-Stefan Landberg, 4-Jonas Olsson, 6-Teddy Lucic, 13-Mikael Nilsson, 9-Niclas Alexandersson (Peter Eriksson, 74) 19-Magnus Erlingmark, 11-Stefan Lindqvist, 16-Jesper Blomqvist, 14-Andreas Andersson (21-Martinsson, 81), 10-Stefan Pettersson.
